citation.description: Step 'Configure tickets merge driver' runs `git config merge.ours.driver true` after worktree add (line 117) and before the merge in the push-retry loop (line 346). Unit test at test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:58-63 asserts production_mount < production_config < first_merge_index.

criteria.criterion: `reconcile-bridge.yml` sets `merge.ours.driver=true` for the tickets worktree before any merge step. Tier: unit workflow-lint assertion.

citation.description: test_reconcile_workflows_provision_the_ours_driver_once asserts: (a) canary has no direct `git config merge.ours.driver` command (lines 54-56), and (b) canary_mount < canary_init < first_merge_index (line 53). Canary workflow confirmed to have `rebar init` at line 146 and no direct driver config.

criteria.criterion: The canary is asserted to obtain the driver via its existing `rebar init` call, so it needs no edit — a regression guard against re-adding the change there. Tier: unit workflow-lint.

citation.description: test_workflow_driver_makes_diverged_bridge_state_local_wins: configured clone runs the workflow driver command, diverges, merges, asserts returncode==0, result is '{"owner":"local"}', no conflict markers, clean git status.

criteria.criterion: A reconverge against a diverged remote in a fresh runner-shaped checkout resolves `.bridge_state/*` local-wins (not a text merge) and produces no conflict markers. Tier: integration in a real temporary git repo mimicking the runner setup.

citation.description: Negative control in the same test: unconfigured clone diverges and merges, asserts returncode != 0 and conflict markers ('<<<<<<< HEAD' and '>>>>>>> remote-pass') present in the bindings file.

criteria.criterion: The same scenario without the config produces the text-merge behaviour — the negative control proving the test detects the defect. Tier: integration.
